findings.claim: The AST widening closes the 'positional reason is invisible' blind spot, so an unregistered positional reason code fails the gate.
findings.counter_evidence: `_signatures` keys callees by BARE NAME and keeps the FIRST definition in sorted-path order (`out.setdefault(node.name, _param_names(node))`, line 68), and `_callee_name` throws away the receiver (line 84-89). Measured with the gate's own helper: gate._signatures(SRC)['_reject'] == ['artifact','reason'] (artifact_handle.py:62 wins over close_gap.py:206 ['reason']); gate._signatures(SRC)['_result'] == ['cls','connection','row'] (evidence_query.py:289 wins over resolver.py:1907 and security_identity.py:576). Consequence, measured: a locally-correct scan of source_catalog finds 49 code-like reason-position sites; 17 are invisible to the gate, and 16 of them carry NEVER-REGISTERED codes - close_gap.py:224 no_runtime_policy, close_gap.py:226 stale_policy_hash (the latter is asserted by an existing contract test, tests/contract/test_close_gap_fc801.py:205 `assert result.reason == 'stale_policy_hash'`), resolver.py:1501/1512/1519/1527/1538/1545/1553/1563 and security_identity.py:622/632/642/667/679/688 - plus stale_gap_hash at close_gap.py:256. End-to-end mutation on a TEMP COPY: `python mut_step.py repl .../close_gap.py stale_gap_hash brand_new_positional_code 1` (i.e. the :256 site) then the gate's own test_every_emitted_reason_is_registered() -> GREEN; the identical rename at the :380 site -> RED "... ['brand_new_positional_code'] - locations: {'brand_new_positional_code': ['close_gap.py:380']}". So a positional drift in close_gap.py / resolver.py / security_identity.py passes CI unnoticed today, and the in-tree evidence already contains 16 such codes.
findings.required_fix: Resolve callees per file/class scope (module-local symbols first, `self`/`cls` stripped for methods), union the candidate signatures of same-named definitions instead of taking the first, and fail closed when two candidates disagree about which index is the reason parameter; then re-run the widened gate and register or rewrite the 16 codes it now reports (and re-check the inventory tool with the same fix).
findings.residual: Even after that fix the literal-only AST scan cannot see runtime-computed reasons (36 non-literal reason positions, e.g. admission.py:271 `_rejected('|'.join(reasons), *reasons)` emits a pipe-joined multi-code string) - that is inherent to the design and should be stated as a limit.

findings.area: evidence / acceptance criteria (repo B evidence + findings.md)
findings.claim: The positional inventory is the actionable, complete list of unregistered codes: '33 positional sites, 32 code-like => 15 codes were never registered' (findings.md:7-8, fc1301-unregistered.txt, fc1301-reason-inventory.json), and acceptance criterion 2 ('every existing reason registered or rewritten, with a per-item disposition') is therefore met.
findings.counter_evidence: The inventory tool has the SAME first-definition-wins resolver as the gate (fc1301_reason_inventory.py:69 `signatures.setdefault(node.name, ...)`), so it reports 0 unregistered code-like positional values while a locally-correct resolution of the same tree finds 16 unregistered code-like SITES (=16 distinct codes) at _reject/_result call sites the tool mis-mapped. fc1301-unregistered.txt lists exactly 40 lines and ends at 'stale_gap_hash @ close_gap.py:380'; the 'unregistered sites' list omits close_gap.py:224, close_gap.py:226 and all 14 resolver/security_identity _result sites. findings.md:7-8 states the 15-code conclusion with a '=>' inference from a scan that cannot see them.
findings.required_fix: Fix the tool's resolution as in B-VR1301-01, regenerate the inventory and the unregistered list, and either register the 16 codes (with per-item semantics and stage) or rewrite the call sites - then restate the acceptance criterion with the new counts.
findings.residual: Whether these 16 codes are IN SCOPE is a scope judgement the owner should make; the registry itself claims to be 'kept in sync with admission/reuse/resolver/artifact codes' (observability.py:33-34), resolver-family codes such as exact_hit/latest_selected/reused_after_discovery/existing_catalog_source_reused_before_adapter ARE registered, and stale_policy_hash sits in the same nested helper as the stale_gap_hash the commit did register - so the case for in-scope is strong but not owner-decided.

findings.claim: The 15 new codes are placed in the right STAGES_BY_REASON buckets ('same stage as the sibling focus_policy_* codes: the decision is made while admitting an artifact').
findings.counter_evidence: The map documents its own attribution rules (observability.py:195-204): identity = 'entity/security identity + admission profile gates', artifact = 'artifact schema/hash/binding/status + path-policy checks', semantic = 'content/meaning-level decisions', freshness = 'as-of date, period, gap analysis, timeliness'. Against those rules: (a) the 13 focus_policy_* codes are title/metadata keyword classification decisions and are staged ('artifact',) while their direct sibling from the same function, focus_policy_no_allowed_category_evidence (admission.py:226, the fall-through of that same keyword ladder), is ('semantic',) - so the comment's premise 'same stage as the sibling focus_policy_* codes' is false; (b) v2_profile_admitted is an admission-profile gate (evaluate_candidate, admission.py:244-276) and is staged ('artifact',), while its sibling `admitted` - whose registry description is nearly identical, 'candidate facts pass the profile gate' - is ('identity',); (c) stale_gap_hash is a gap-plan revalidation (close_gap.py:247-256 / 372-380, 'gap revalidation (DL-03) - metadata only, nothing fetched') and is staged ('acquisition',), while the codes in the same if-block, gap_already_closed and gap_closed_by_concurrent, are both ('freshness',). Consequence: _reason_stage_problems (observability.py:404-409) fails closed, so an event emitted under the natural stage is dropped by MetricsCollector.record_stage_event, and the map is documented as consumed cross-repo ('revenue-forecast and filing-fetch consume this map in later cards').
findings.required_fix: Re-derive the stage for each of the 15 codes from the documented attribution rules (most plausibly semantic/identity for the focus_policy_* batch, identity for v2_profile_admitted, freshness for stale_gap_hash), and correct the in-code justification comment.
findings.residual: No production emitter of StageEvent exists in src yet (callers are tests and scripts), so the impact is latent - but it lands on the cross-repo consumers the map is written for.

findings.claim: The gate validates the registry of the tree it scans.
findings.counter_evidence: The gate computes SRC = <test>/../../src/company_wiki/source_catalog and then does `sys.path.insert(0, str(SRC.parent))`, i.e. it inserts ...\src\company_wiki - a directory that provably contains no `company_wiki` package (verified: (SRC.parent/'company_wiki').is_dir() is False; the directory holds __init__.py, automation/, canonical_ingest.py, ...). The import therefore resolves through whatever `company_wiki` is installed: with company-wiki paths removed from sys.path, `import company_wiki` raises ImportError; in this environment a .pth/editable entry supplies repo A. Demonstrated impact: running the gate against a COPY of the tree with a dropped registration printed registry_file = repo A's observability.py and GREEN (registry_is_the_copy=false); only after I forced the copy's src onto sys.path did the same mutation produce the claimed RED. Repo B's inventory tool guards against exactly this (fc1301_reason_inventory.py:228-231 'imported a DIFFERENT copy of the registry'); the CI gate does not.
findings.required_fix: Insert the correct path (SRC.parents[1]) and add the inventory tool's registry-identity assertion (imported observability.__file__ must equal the scanned tree's observability.py), so a mismatch is red instead of silently green.
findings.residual: In CI (checkout + editable install of the same tree) both paths coincide, so today's CI result is probably unaffected; the risk is to copy-based verification and to any installed-package environment.

notes: Method: read-only git + file reads + text search + SHA-256 + Python ast; three independent scanners written in %TEMP%\vr1301 (union-resolution, per-file local-resolution, and a fixture harness that calls the gate's own emitted_codes()), plus an isolated-process mutation harness on a COPY of src/company_wiki. Repo A was never written: `git status --porcelain` in company-wiki is empty and HEAD is still 76cc1bcd936ad3cd48e4f150f3683fd1bd346a4f. Errors I made and corrected: (1) my first mutation harness ran all mutations in one interpreter, so the cached company_wiki.source_catalog.observability module made the dropped-registration mutation report GREEN - corrected by one process per step; (2) my second attempt still imported repo A's registry because an editable install (.pth / _EditableFinder) put it on sys.path ahead of the copy, while the gate's own `sys.path.insert(0, str(SRC.parent))` points at a directory that cannot contain the package - I detected this with an explicit registry-identity printout and fixed it by stripping the editable finder and the installed path, which is how B-VR1301-04 was found; (3) a PowerShell argument-quoting problem mangled a mutation anchor ('anchor not found'), so the anchors were moved inside the script; (4) my first fixture script crashed on a missing parent directory (FileNotFoundError) - fixed with mkdir; (5) my first independent scanner used a union-of-all-same-named-definitions model, which over-approximated reason indices (36 'non-literal' hits, some belonging to a different same-named definition), so I added the per-file local-resolution model and report the 49-sites / 17-invisible / 16-unregistered numbers from that stricter model.
